senses.gloss:
laya
(‘dissolution’)
------------------------------------------
Derived from the root ‘lī’ (to dissolve, to disappear) the word ‘laya’ has been used in several senses.
When it refers to the dissolution of the created world (for e.g., सृष्टि, sthiti and लय), the term ‘pralaya’ is more frequently used. (See PRALAYA for details.)
In the works on योग, it refers to the समाधि state wherein the मिन्द् is completely merged in the object of meditation.
In Advaita Vedānta, it is considered as the first obstacle to the realisation of आत्मन्, the others being विक्षेप (distraction), कषाय (failure to rest on the आत्मन् due to attachments) and rasāsvāda (enjoying the taste of bliss in lower समाधि). Here, लय is the relapsing of the मिन्द् into sleep instead of meditating on the आत्मन्.
In मुसिच् it refers to the maintenance of the speed with which a song is begun to be sung.

layayoga
(‘yoga of dissolution [of the मिन्द् in ब्रह्मन्]’)
------------------------------------------
Out of the several systems of योग mentioned in the works on योग, लययोग also is one.
Laya or dissolution of the individual चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स् is achieved when प्रकृति (Mother Nature, same as the कुण्डलिनी) is taken up from the mūlādhāracakra (the lowest plexus), step by step, right up to the सहस्रार (the ‘thousand-petalled lotus’) where it is merged in पुरुष or ब्रह्मन्. This is called ‘Layayoga’.
According to some works on योग like the Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa Upaniṣad (5.1-5), लययोग comprises nine steps: यम (restraint), नियम (culture), sthūlakriyā (gross practices like the āsanas), sūkṣma kriyā (subtle practices like प्राणायाम), प्रत्याहार (withdrawal of senses), धारणा (fixed attention), ध्यान (meditation), layakriyā (act of dissolution of the मिन्द् into ब्रह्मन्) and समाधि or महालय (final dissolution resulting in the losing of one’s personality into that of ब्रह्मन्).
Mokṣa or लिबेरतिओन् from transmigratory existence results from this.
